sources.extract: Reveals misconceptions at low cost; caveats: no detailed statistics, unnatural speech, facilitator prompts can bias behaviour.

sources.title: MDN - StorageManager.persist()
sources.extract: Resolves true if storage is made persistent, else false; the browser decides; secure contexts; not in Workers.

sources.title: MDN - Storage quotas and eviction criteria
sources.extract: Best-effort data can be evicted LRU; persistent data only by user action; Firefox prompts, others decide silently; Safari may delete script-created data after 7 days.

sources.title: City of Vancouver Open Data - Public streets (API records)
sources.extract: Street segments as GeoJSON. Our computation: Granville St about 44.6 deg and W Georgia St about 134-135 deg from true north. Licence page opened in r3 shows only a heading and links to the terms of use; no licence text.

sources.title: Vancouver's deviant grids (Villagomez)
sources.extract: Describes a 45 degree grid of the city centre; qualitative, not a surveyed angle.

sources.title: UBC SALA home page
sources.publisher: UBC School of Architecture and Landscape Architecture
sources.extract: Land acknowledgement and commitment to reconciliation; no Indigenous advisory body or contact found; UBC Indigenous portal URLs redirected to a status page on 21 Oct 2026.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.extract: Recommendation of 30 Apr 2013; Entity, Activity, Agent (Person, SoftwareAgent); wasAttributedTo, wasGeneratedBy, actedOnBehalfOf (first 100,000 characters read).

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.1 Use of Color
sources.extract: Colour must not be the only visual means of conveying information (Level A); text cues, patterns and icons are techniques.

sources.title: TCPS 2 (2022) Chapter 2, Article 2.5
sources.extract: Quality assurance, program evaluation and testing within normal educational requirements are not research when used only for improvement; later research use may need REB review. UBC's own rule not read.

sources.extract: Read locally 21 Oct 2026. Schema v0 with semver schema_version and vN to vN+1 migrations; street axes 44.7 and 134.7 deg; core 21.0 person-days against 34 nominal to 13 Nov (slice 19.5 against 26 to 6 Nov); proposes Apache-2.0 and DCO 1.1; deadlines stored in UTC. Internal, not reachable by outsiders; the folder is not a git repository, so no commit hash exists yet.

sources.title: exifr README
sources.extract: MIT; described as an EXIF reading library; API parse, gps, orientation, rotation, thumbnail, sidecar; no write or strip function; reads EXIF, XMP, ICC, IPTC, JFIF from JPEG, TIFF, PNG, HEIC, AVIF.

sources.title: Wikipedia - JPEG (syntax and structure)
sources.extract: Marker table: SOI FFD8, SOFn, DHT FFC4, DQT FFDB, DRI FFDD, SOS FFDA, RSTn FFD0-D7, APPn FFE0-EF, COM FFFE, EOI FFD9; two-byte length counts itself. First 100,000 of 216,837 characters read.

sources.title: ExifTool - JPEG tags
sources.extract: APP0 JFIF/JFXX; APP1 Exif, XMP, ExtendedXMP; APP2 ICC_Profile, FlashPix, MPF; APP13 Photoshop; APP14 Adobe; COM comment. IPTC in APP13 is not named on the page.

sources.title: ExifTool - EXIF tags
sources.extract: IFD1 lists ThumbnailOffset (0x0201) and ThumbnailLength (0x0202), so an Exif block can carry a thumbnail. The page does not say thumbnails retain earlier-edit data.

sources.title: jsep - JavaScript expression parser
sources.extract: MIT; a parser that parses expressions but does not evaluate; output almost identical to esprima's. npm 1.6.0 MIT. The AST node list and any security notes are not on the page read.

sources.title: OWASP - Prototype Pollution Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.extract: Use Map or Set; Object.create(null); freeze built-in prototypes (shallow); Object.seal is not enough; Node --disable-proto=delete is defence in depth only. Key rejection and schema validation are not on the page.

sources.title: Apache License 2.0 text
sources.extract: Section 4: give recipients a copy of the licence, mark modified files, keep notices; 4(d) a distributed NOTICE file's attribution notices must be included in a NOTICE file, documentation or a display.

sources.title: MDN - Window.postMessage()
sources.extract: Give a specific targetOrigin, not '*', except for opaque-origin data: URLs; check event.origin and event.source and validate data; transferred ports reach the receiver via MessageEvent.ports. Sandboxed-iframe 'null' origin not covered.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures
sources.extract: Level A: multipoint or path-based gestures need a single-pointer alternative; pinch-zoom is a multipoint gesture and zoom buttons satisfy it; essential exception only; dragging falls under 2.5.7.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
sources.extract: Level AA: author-created content (sticky headers, footers, non-modal dialogs) must not completely hide a focused component; partial overlap allowed; scroll padding is a technique.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible
sources.extract: Level AA: a keyboard-operable interface needs a visible focus indicator that stays visible while focused.

sources.title: tesseract.js - local installation guide
sources.extract: Core WASM and language data load from the jsDelivr CDN by default; workerPath, corePath and langPath let you self-host; the default worker location is not stated.

sources.title: Sigstore - Signing blobs with cosign
sources.extract: Keyless 'cosign sign-blob FILE --bundle bundle.sigstore.json' ties an ephemeral key to an OIDC identity; the bundle holds signature, certificate and log proof. Verification is on another page (not read).

flags.claim: Pyodide/WebAssembly isolation is enough to run untrusted community Python safely in the browser.
flags.correction: Treat Pyodide as one layer only. A 7 Aug 2026 disclosure showed escapes in seven products. Add host-level isolation (separate origin, CSP on the sandbox document, no network), allowlists, stripped exports, maintainer review, or run server-side.
flags.detail: WebAssembly's own docs list side channels and in-memory overflows as remaining risks; corrected in r1 to four of seven products with no code fix.

flags.claim: A Web Worker created by our page inherits the page's Content-Security-Policy and is therefore a safe place for community code.
flags.correction: Workers are generally not governed by the creating document's CSP; a worker script needs its own CSP header (blob: and data: workers inherit). Workers also keep network access unless blocked.
flags.detail: MDN: a page with script-src 'self' blocks eval(), yet code in a worker it creates can still call eval().

flags.claim: litegraph.js (or its Comfy fork) is a maintained, safe choice for the node canvas.
flags.correction: Original litegraph.js last pushed 2024-08-01 with about 1.2 k weekly downloads; the Comfy-Org fork is archived (2026-01-14). Use @xyflow/react (pushed 2026-10-20, about 8.3 M weekly downloads) with Rete as fallback.
flags.detail: Observed 21 Oct 2026 from GitHub API and npm download API.

flags.claim: A keyboard alternative satisfies the drag requirement ('Single-pointer or keyboard alternative to drag', WCAG 2.5.7).
flags.correction: Provide single-pointer, non-drag alternatives (click source then target, numeric fields) and test keyboard operability separately under SC 2.1.1.
flags.detail: The Understanding page says keyboard equivalence does not automatically meet SC 2.5.7 and the two are evaluated independently (P15-S50). Scope widened in r2 and r3.

flags.claim: A sandboxed community worker can carry its own CSP response header (connect-src none) inside an opaque-origin iframe, with the sandbox hosted on GitHub Pages.
flags.correction: Put the CSP and the sandbox directive on the sandbox iframe document's response header, on a header-capable separate domain; the blob worker inherits it. Test denial of fetch, WebSocket, importScripts, nested Worker, eval and top navigation in three engines.
flags.detail: MDN: blob and data workers inherit the creator's CSP (P15-S18); GitHub Pages cannot set headers (P15-S27). Worker creation from an opaque origin stays unverified.

flags.claim: INP thresholds are 'verified' for measuring canvas interaction latency in a test build at the 75th percentile.
flags.correction: Reclassified as team_assumption. Use a scripted interaction set and report Event Timing p98 per session.
flags.detail: web.dev defines the bands at the 75th percentile of field page loads; lab INP depends on which interactions are scripted (P15-S47). Method corrected again in r2.

flags.claim: The VTC terms say nothing that restricts redistribution of competition materials, and only anonymity constrains entrants' publishing.
flags.correction: Never host Buildner's Presentation Template Package in modules or templates. Treat sharing design visuals before judging as a risk under 4.1, and keep projects local by default.
flags.detail: Terms 7.5.5 forbid redistribution of the template package; 7.5.6 keeps organiser IP; 4.1 requires unpublished visuals (P15-S60, P15-S80). 'Published' is undefined.

flags.claim: Whether giscus needs a public repository is unknown.
flags.correction: giscus requires a public repository with the app installed and Discussions enabled, so all comments are public and tied to GitHub accounts; module-page threads only, with a privacy notice.
flags.detail: giscus.app states the repository must be public (P15-S64).

flags.claim: npm provenance provides signed provenance for registry module bundles.
flags.correction: Use GitHub artifact attestations (actions/attest) on bundle files, verify them in CI, and have the client check the index SHA-256; mirror accepted bundles.
flags.detail: npm provenance is generated by npm publish --provenance for npm packages; bundles at URLs are not npm packages (P15-S40, P15-S70, P15-S71).

flags.claim: Two of the seven products in the Aug 2026 Pyodide disclosure received no fix.
flags.correction: Four of seven (cohere-terrarium, langchain-sandbox, stlite, cibuildwheel) had no code fix; the three fixes that shipped moved or removed in-process Pyodide. T3 is the Python default; browser Pyodide is a dev tier.
flags.detail: Cyera status table read 21 Oct 2026 (P15-S17).

flags.claim: Scripting a drag and recording Event Timing durations measures canvas drag latency (M01, M02 and M04 latency metrics).
flags.correction: Use Event Timing (durationThreshold 16 ms) only for discrete interactions, p98 over all scripted interactions with unreported ones counted as 16 ms. Measure drag, pan and zoom as frame times.
flags.detail: W3C Event Timing lists mousemove, pointermove, touchmove, wheel and drag as continuous events that are not exposed (P15-S87, P15-S88).

flags.claim: Incremental re-run bands (good <= 5 s, bad > 30 s) have no sourced benchmark (M02).
flags.correction: Rebase on Nielsen's limits: good <= 1 s for T0 and formula nodes, acceptable <= 10 s, bad > 10 s unless a percent-done indicator and Cancel are shown; a sourced guideline applied by our reading.
flags.detail: Nielsen (1993, updated 2014): 0.1, 1 and 10 s limits (P15-S86).

flags.claim: Connect, move and resize are the drag actions needing single-pointer alternatives (M01 SC 2.5.7 metric).
flags.correction: Inventory all drag props: pan, edge reconnect, marquee and minimap pan too; give each a click alternative or disable it, and test by enumerating enabled props.
flags.detail: React Flow defaults panOnDrag true and edgesReconnectable true (P15-S77); MiniMap pannable is a drag (P15-S91). Widened again in r3.

flags.claim: Longest-list matching is design logic supported by P15-S12.
flags.correction: Cite McNeel's data-stream-matching page (P15-S90) for the documented default, stamp repeated items, offer strict matching for metric nodes. r3: that page is a 2020 Explicit History labs page, so Grasshopper's own default stays unverified.
flags.detail: P15-S12 covers data trees only. Silent repetition can create a pass/fail result nobody asked for.

flags.claim: About 3 dev-weeks of capacity are available for P15 core before 13 Nov (r2 schedule flag).
flags.correction: P14 core is 21.0 person-days (62% of nominal 34 to 13 Nov; its 19.5 slice is 75% of 26 to 6 Nov). P15 core is re-baselined to 12.0 person-days (never-cut minimum 7.0); 21.0 + 12.0 = 33.0 of 34 before P13 and P16 are counted.
flags.detail: The critique's '75% of 26 to 13 Nov' mixes the two P14 figures; its conclusion holds. P13 core slices sum to about 30.5 and P16's 13 Nov slices to about 10.5 person-days (our sums of stated figures, P15-S125, P15-S126), against the same two students. A cross-packet capacity table needs a team decision.

flags.claim: The core export flow strips author, team and path metadata using the listed library (exifr).
flags.correction: exifr only reads. Core uses a first-party lossless allow-list JPEG segment rewriter, a re-scan, a size check and a stamp bound to the post-strip hash. PDF leaves core (VTC panels are JPEG).
flags.detail: exifr README: a reading library; API parse, gps, orientation, rotation, thumbnail, sidecar (P15-S109). Re-encoding through canvas would alter pixels, ICC and size against the 10 MB cap.

flags.claim: Setting selectionOnDrag off removes marquee drag, and shift-click can serve as the multi-select alternative.
flags.correction: Set selectionKeyCode to null (default 'Shift' still draws a selection box) and use outline checkboxes; the default multi-select key is Control or Meta, not Shift. Add pinch (SC 2.5.1) with Controls zoom buttons.
flags.detail: React Flow API page re-read in r3: selectionKeyCode 'Shift', multiSelectionKeyCode Control/Meta, zoomOnPinch true; passing null disables key props (P15-S77, P15-S119).

flags.claim: The SemVer compliance metric (MINOR inside 0.y.z counts as breaking) is 'verified', and other policy thresholds (licence field OSI rule, CI gate, SemVer detection, community profile, pointer target size) were verified.
flags.correction: Relabelled team_assumption with the verified part kept in the basis: SemVer item 4 says only that 0.y.z may change; the MINOR rule is the node-semver caret convention.
flags.detail: Six metrics relabelled in r3 (M01 pointer target size, M03 SemVer and licence field, M05 CI gate and SemVer detection, M08 community profile).

flags.claim: T0 declarative modules need no code execution and are therefore safe before the sandbox ships.
flags.correction: T0 expressions arrive in imported JSON, so the evaluator is attack surface: allow-list grammar, caps, worker with deadline, Ajv-validated imports without prototype keys, fuzz suite. mathjs is dropped from core.
flags.detail: mathjs docs warn of unknown parser vulnerabilities and advise a killable worker (P15-S84); OWASP lists prototype pollution mitigations (P15-S114).

flags.claim: Storing a named actor with every decided_by value is harmless to VTC anonymity.
flags.correction: Actors are local pseudonyms (member-A); the name map stays on the device and is excluded from every exporter; RunRecord and graph JSON join the scan scope; environment blocks omit user, host and path.
flags.detail: Terms 5.1 and 5.3 hide identities until winners are chosen; a name in a provenance table on a board would pass a metadata-only scan (P15-S60).

flags.claim: MIT licensing of React Flow means the on-canvas attribution can be removed without paying.
flags.detail: The vendor states attribution may be removed only with a Pro subscription while the library stays MIT. Whether MIT legally obliges the badge was not verified; default is to leave it visible. Whether exports need the badge is also unverified.

flags.claim: The Contributor Covenant text is CC BY 4.0.
flags.correction: Version 3.0 states CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike). Decision: adopt 3.0 with a CC BY-SA attribution notice and its own licence-matrix row.
flags.detail: The 2.1 page states no licence (P15-S83).

flags.claim: Editable presets without literature source: Event Timing p98 bands; frame time p95 16.7 / 33.3 ms; T0 caps (500 characters, depth 32, 256 nodes, 1 s); debounce 250 ms; response-time and block-time bands; Wilson 0.80 / 0.50 with n >= 5; Scorecard 7 / 4; library maintained = pushed within 90 days; extracts <= 25 words; expert badge >= 2 reviewers; <= 8 hue families; backup <= 24 h; output caps and cross-engine tolerances after benchmarking.
flags.detail: Shown in the tool as editable team assumptions per the course rule. In r3 each carries decided_by role ai, unconfirmed, until a named student confirms it.

flags.claim: Usability bands (task success >= 80% good / < 50% bad; first result <= 15 min / > 30 min; wiring errors <= 1 / >= 3; chip comprehension >= 90% / < 70%; provenance >= 80% / < 50%; stale recognition >= 90% / < 70%; graph explained by >= 4 of 5 reviewers) and the 5-8 participant plan.
flags.detail: No sourced band exists for node editors; Nielsen's five-user figure supports the sample logic only (P15-S98).

flags.claim: decided_by rule: AI-drafted values cannot be 'verified' until a named person confirms them; every parameter, threshold and metric carries code, ai or person with a pseudonymous actor and date.
flags.detail: Derived from the course rule; PROV agent types are the model (P15-S105). r3 applies it to this packet: 91 metrics and 17 numeric-preset parameters carry role ai, unconfirmed; no student has confirmed any yet.

flags.claim: React Flow node/edge capacity at 60 fps; Pyodide cold-start time; COEP side effects on embeds; GitHub API rate limits; handle shrinkage under canvas zoom; mutability of GitHub release assets; attestation availability by plan; whether React Flow pans a focused node out from under overlays.
flags.detail: No sourced figures found; each needs a benchmark or a read of the documentation. r3 re-read two GitHub attestation pages: neither states plan eligibility; cosign keyless is the fallback (P15-S123).

flags.claim: A blob Worker can be started inside an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is enough CSP for QuickJS-WASM and Pyodide, and a CSP hash source works in such a document.
flags.detail: MDN confirms CSP inheritance, the sandbox header and the keyword, not worker creation from an opaque origin or minimum CSP per runtime. The CI denial suite decides; fallback design B serves the page on a separate registrable domain with its own worker CSP header.

flags.claim: The street-grid bearing (about 44.7 deg and 134.7 deg from true north) and the true-north frame of the VTC block itself.
flags.detail: P14-M03 derives 44.7 deg from 969 parcels (internal); r2 computed 44.6 deg (Granville St) and about 134-135 deg (W Georgia St) from City segments (P15-S102). Spacing says only '45 degree grid' (P15-S103). The site plan arrow was not opened.

flags.claim: Long Animation Frames are available outside Chromium.
flags.detail: The MDN page gives the 50 ms threshold but no compatibility table (P15-S89). Frame time rests on requestAnimationFrame deltas.

flags.claim: Target designers expect Grasshopper-style recompute-on-change, so auto mode is the right default for T0 nodes.
flags.detail: The McNeel guide index did not describe solver recompute. r3 moves auto mode to v1; the pilot (P15-M09) tests whether run-all plus stale hatch is enough.

flags.claim: React Flow keyboard connection, handle focus and Controls button labels.
flags.detail: The accessibility, API and Controls pages do not document them (P15-S76, P15-S94); the outline view and our own labels supply them. Needs a browser test.

flags.claim: Grant rate of navigator.storage.persist() per browser and whether Safari's 7-day deletion covers OPFS.
flags.detail: MDN gives eviction rules but no rates and does not name OPFS for the Safari rule (P15-S100, P15-S101).

flags.claim: Whether the VTC results date of 26 Jan 2027 will hold, and whether the upload cutoff is 23:59 or 24:00 London time.
flags.detail: r3: the competition page lists results 26 Jan 2027 and submission 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London time = 15:59 in Vancouver (GMT, UTC-8) (P15-S82). The r2 reading of the terms says '24.00'; the r3 re-fetch of the terms failed (timeouts, HTTP 502). Use the earlier time; terms 10.7 allow extension, so the embargo end stays entrant-set (suggested 26 Jan 2027).

flags.claim: Whether UBC requires REB review for think-aloud sessions run for this course project.
flags.detail: TCPS 2 Article 2.5 exempts quality-improvement use (P15-S107), but UBC's own policy was not read. Ask the course team before recruiting.

flags.claim: Green and Petre (1996) as a directly read source.
flags.detail: The DOI redirected to a page with no text; definitions come from the opened Green and Blackwell tutorial (P15-S97).

flags.claim: City of Vancouver open-data licence text and attribution rules for datasets other modules may import (including public-streets).
flags.detail: r3: the licence page shows only the heading 'Open data licence' and links to terms of use; no licence text. P14 cites an Open Government Licence - Vancouver page it read (P14-S78). Needs a manual check before any dataset is redistributed.

flags.claim: Whether the VTC brief PDF, site plan and 3D model may be redistributed inside the registry.
flags.detail: Terms 7.5.5 bar redistribution of the Presentation Template Package only; the download sits behind an email form. Policy until clarified: link and cite only, do not host.

flags.claim: What counts as 'previously published' under VTC terms 4.1 (a private link, a public repository, a social post).
flags.detail: The FAQ and resubmission page allow reuse with visually updated materials; no clause on social media. Ask Buildner before enabling any public sharing; the publish gate stays on.

flags.claim: Who qualifies as an expert reviewer for the expert-reviewed badge, and who stands behind it.
flags.detail: Needs a governance decision with the course team; rOpenSci and JOSS show the process but not a qualification standard.

flags.claim: Indigenous governance route: Nation-authorised involvement for content touching Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh knowledge; OCAP and the City UNDRIP pages; owner of the SALA contact.
flags.detail: OCAP and the City UNDRIP page returned 403 again (third round, no archive used). SALA's home page has a land acknowledgement but no advisory body or contact (P15-S104). The owner name for the 4 Nov contact is not in the materials; the team must record it this week. Content stays held.

flags.claim: Person who owns the Layer 0 schema freeze and the date; deprecation policy for versioned port types; pilot facilitator.
flags.detail: P14 owns the schema (P15-S108); no person is named in the materials for the freeze (team target 1 Nov, fallback 28 Oct: P15 maintainers freeze) or for the pilot. P14 is at schema v0 with migration fixtures; proposal: tag 1.0.0 at the freeze so MINOR becomes additive. Team to name owners by 23 Oct.

flags.claim: Overlap of P14-M06 and P13-M06v with P15-M07 (versioning, provenance, anonymised export, board JPEG scan).
flags.detail: P14-M06 plans snapshots and anonymised export; P13-M06v validates board JPEGs (metadata scan, OCR deny-list, sha256 manifest) (P15-S125). P15-M07 core is the interim implementation for non-board exports; one owner and one stamp format are needed. Decision between packet owners.

flags.claim: Core hosting and CSP delivery: which host serves the app and whether it can send headers.
flags.detail: Not named in the materials. GitHub Pages cannot send headers (P15-S27), so only the meta CSP applies (no frame-ancestors, no report-only); Cloudflare Pages _headers can (P15-S78). Whether React Flow needs style-src 'unsafe-inline' is unverified. The team names the host.

flags.claim: Project code licence, contributor sign-off and ownership between the two students.
flags.detail: P14 proposes Apache-2.0 and DCO 1.1 for ratification before the first public upload (P15-S108, P15-S117). UBC's student software ownership rule was not found on page 1 of 5 of the policy repository (P15-S124). A person must ratify and check.

flags.claim: UBC privacy impact and data-residency check for any future server-side storage of projects or comments (GitHub is US-hosted).
flags.detail: Not checked; the local-first default avoids server storage of designs, so the check is deferred until a server option is proposed.

flags.claim: JPEG details: IPTC inside APP13, identifying text in ICC profile description or copyright tags, and trailing data after EOI (MPF, thumbnails).
flags.detail: The exiftool page lists APP13 Photoshop but not IPTC (P15-S111); ICC text fields and trailing data are not on the pages read. The rewriter drops APP13 and trailing bytes and keeps ICC only if allow-listed; fixtures decide.

flags.claim: Schedule r3: core re-baselined to about 12.0 person-days (M01 3.0, M02 2.0, M03 3.0, M07 1.5, M08 1.0, M09 1.5), never-cut minimum about 7.0; P14 core is 21.0 against nominal 34 to 13 Nov.
flags.detail: r2 had about 16.5 person-days. Moved to v1: T0 auto mode, trees, minimap, step-into, PDF scan, OCR. Capacity of the two students (nominal 34 to 13 Nov, 26 to 6 Nov) is assumed; P13 (about 30.5) and P16 (about 10.5) slices are on top. If the cross-packet plan does not fit, the first-run notice shows a later date.

flags.claim: Food4Rhino moderation, rating and publishing practices, and Dynamo run-mode behaviour.
flags.detail: Food4Rhino returned HTTP 403; the Dynamo primer pages did not cover run modes. Neither is used as evidence in any threshold.

unresolved_relationships: Graph size (node and edge count) vs canvas frame time and recompute time in React Flow: the performance guide gives no figures; needs a benchmark.
Frame-time bands (p95 <= 16.7 ms good, > 33.3 ms bad) vs perceived smoothness on mid-range laptops: no sourced band for node-editor drag.
Pyodide package set and cold-start time vs user abandonment: no sourced numbers.
Number of expert reviewers vs defect escape rate for community modules: rOpenSci uses two but gives no evidence of the optimum.
Rating count and Wilson score vs actual module correctness: the statistic handles sampling uncertainty only.
Review response time vs contributor retention in a student-run registry: CHAOSS gives no numeric relationship.
Sandbox permission granularity vs contributor and user friction: no sourced evidence.
Run-all-only core with a stale hatch vs stale-number misreading and trust: no sourced evidence; tested in the P15-M09 pilot.
Auto debounce length (v1 preset 250 ms) vs wasted re-runs and perceived instantness: Nielsen gives the 0.1 s and 1 s limits but no debounce value.
Longest-list repetition vs rate of silent pass/fail errors in metric nodes: McNeel's 2020 Explicit History page documents the behaviour, no error-rate data; Grasshopper's own default unverified.
Template granularity (nodes per template) vs reuse and learning: no sourced evidence.
Disabled-node mode (bypass vs block) vs correctness of downstream verdicts: design logic only.
Effect of COEP require-corp or credentialless on third-party embeds (giscus, map tiles) and on Pyodide interrupts: not verified.
Canvas zoom level vs rendered handle size (minZoom default 0.5) and the zoom threshold below which handles hide: inferred, needs measurement against WCAG 2.5.8.
Number of category hue families (13 codes, cap 8 plus lightness) vs distinguishability under colour-vision deficiency: no sourced limit; text codes carry the meaning.
Designer comprehension of status chips, the corrected-history icon and the decided_by strip vs misuse of evidence: untested until the P15-M09 pilot.
Wiring-error rate and time to first result for M.Arch designers on the starter graph: no data until the pilot.
Minimum CSP that QuickJS-WASM and Pyodide need to start, and whether CSP hash sources work in an opaque-origin document: settle in the CI denial suite.
Whether an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe can start a blob Worker in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: inferred, not verified.
Cross-engine numeric differences in module outputs vs the tolerance needed per metric type: ECMAScript allows approximation but no sourced magnitudes.
Output size and list-length caps vs memory exhaustion or rendering freeze: no sourced figures; benchmark.
T0 caps (500 characters, depth 32, 256 nodes, 1 s) vs legitimate module formulas: presets untested; the fuzz suite and starter graph show whether they bind.
Graph size vs RunRecord size and export time: no sourced figures.
Whether sharing work-in-progress visuals (private link, public repository, social post) counts as 'previously published' under VTC 4.1: terms undefined; ask Buildner.
Time from vulnerability report to client-side block vs exposure of users with the module in their lockfiles: no sourced benchmark.
Local-first storage eviction and clearing vs risk of losing a design: MDN gives eviction rules but no rates; persist() grant rate per browser is unknown.

case_studies.tool: Grasshopper ecosystem: Yak package manager and Food4Rhino
case_studies.what_it_does: Yak packages Grasshopper plug-ins with a manifest.yml, installs them through Rhino's Package Manager, and lets owners push versions that cannot be overwritten, only yanked. Food4Rhino is the named community download site.
case_studies.workflow_step: Distribution and discovery of analysis plug-ins
case_studies.how_used: Designers find a plug-in, install it, wire it into a definition by hand.
case_studies.strengths: Simple manifest, SemVer or four-digit versions, immutable versions with yank, ownership by first pusher.
case_studies.stops_at: The Yak push page describes no review or moderation step and no sandbox; it records no per-threshold sources or assumptions. Food4Rhino could not be opened.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Automated manifest lint, source-link checking and test running before listing.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Judging whether a plug-in's thresholds are right for Vancouver policy.

case_studies.what_it_does: Public registry of custom nodes with semantic versioning, immutable versions, deprecation, unique names, malicious-behaviour scanning with a verification flag, and workflow JSON that stores node versions.
case_studies.how_used: Users install nodes through ComfyUI-Manager and share workflows.
case_studies.strengths: Closest precedent for a node canvas with community modules, versioned workflows and a security verification flag.
case_studies.stops_at: Scanning looks for patterns such as custom pip wheels and system calls; the page does not claim it proves safety or describe runtime sandboxing.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Pattern-based scanning and triage of new versions.

case_studies.what_it_does: Plugins ship README, LICENSE and manifest.json; version must match the release tag; ids are unique; automatic review blocks installation until errors are fixed.
case_studies.how_used: Author publishes a GitHub release, submits, fixes automated review errors.
case_studies.stops_at: Automatic review only; no human expert review or sandbox is described.

case_studies.what_it_does: Taps are git repositories of formulae installable by name; homebrew-core accepts changes by pull request with CI, organisation-member approval and bot merge; AI/LLM use must be disclosed.
case_studies.workflow_step: Index repository, PR review, forks and third-party taps
case_studies.how_used: Maintainers review PRs; users add third-party taps and must trust them.
case_studies.strengths: Reviewable git history, CI gate, clear maintainer approval, tap model for unofficial sources.
case_studies.stops_at: Non-official taps rely on user trust; the pages do not describe sandboxing of formula code.

case_studies.tool: rOpenSci software peer review and JOSS
case_studies.what_it_does: Public expert peer review of software: rOpenSci uses two external reviewers and a badge linking to the review thread; JOSS checks OSI licence, tests, documentation and development history.
case_studies.how_used: Authors submit; reviewers work through a checklist in a public GitHub thread.
case_studies.strengths: Transparent, named reviewers, badge points to evidence.
case_studies.stops_at: Neither source defines reviewer qualifications we can copy; both review software quality, not architectural correctness.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Pre-filling the checklist (licence, tests, links) for reviewers.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Expert judgment on wind, structure or planning thresholds.

case_studies.tool: Node-canvas libraries: React Flow (xyflow) vs Rete vs Baklava vs litegraph
case_studies.what_it_does: React Flow renders custom nodes, handles and validation hooks; Rete adds a pull-based dataflow engine with caching; Baklava is Vue-based with an engine and interface types; litegraph.js is canvas-based with typed slots.
case_studies.how_used: Embedded as the editor and, for Rete and Baklava, the engine.
case_studies.strengths: All MIT. xyflow has by far the largest use (about 8.3 M weekly downloads), active pushes, click-to-connect on by default and documented keyboard focus and arrow-key moves; Rete has a cached dataflow engine.
case_studies.stops_at: React Flow has no execution engine or domain port typing, documents no keyboard connect, and enables panOnDrag, edgesReconnectable, Shift selection box and pinch zoom by default; its validation hook guards UI wiring only; litegraph.js is stale and its Comfy fork archived.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Deciding what the port-type vocabulary should be.
case_studies.license_cost: MIT for all four; React Flow Pro is optional and starts at $169/month for attribution removal.

case_studies.tool: Grasshopper visual scripts in practice (Davis, Burry and Burry study)
case_studies.what_it_does: Survey of 1,982 shared Grasshopper scripts plus think-aloud tests with four architecture students comparing modular and unstructured scripts.
case_studies.workflow_step: Reading and modifying someone else's visual graph
case_studies.how_used: Designers share scripts on a forum; peers must understand them to modify them.
case_studies.strengths: Shows what helps legibility: modules, clear names, inputs left and outputs right, colour separation; supplies a think-aloud method for architects.
case_studies.stops_at: Four students and Grasshopper only; no test of status chips, provenance or evidence tools; inline explanations were seldom read.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Suggesting group labels and parameter names from node behaviour.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: Whether a graph expresses the designer's intent.
